pairings.label: Dorms near dining
pairings.line: A short walk to breakfast is the difference between breakfast and not.

pairings.label: Labs near their hall
pairings.line: Nobody carries a tray of specimens across a campus twice.

pairings.label: Recreation near the fields
pairings.line: Changing rooms on one side of the grounds and the grounds on the other is a design nobody defends.

pairings.label: Health near the dorms
pairings.line: The infirmary is only reassuring if you can reach it in a dressing gown.

pairings.label: The library among the halls
pairings.line: A library at the edge of campus is a very quiet library.

pairings.label: Student life near the dorms
pairings.line: The student centre wants to be somewhere people pass, not somewhere they set out for.

readings.placement: Everything the layout is worth, added up and then capped: no arrangement of buildings may move an outcome more than the cap allows.
readings.cap: The hard cap on placement: a college that ignores its layout entirely must stay fully viable, so the total is clamped.
readings.quads: Open spaces the buildings enclose: greener and better enclosed is worth more, and three good ones is a full mark.
readings.enclosure: How much of this quad's edge is built wall. A doorway, water or a road bounds the space without enclosing it; paving encloses it, for less than a wall does.
readings.green: How much of the quad is lawn and trees rather than paving.
readings.quadWorth: What this quad is worth toward campus beauty: its enclosure, lifted by how green it is. A few good ones make a full mark.
readings.pairings: Buildings that belong near each other: the share of each kind that has its partner within a short walk.
readings.beautySwing: What campus beauty is worth to the students' mood, before the cap.

lines.noQuads: No quads yet: three or four buildings around an open space make one.
